hot.title: Masked Visual Actions for Unified World Modeling
hot.summary: Researchers from Stanford University and collaborators developed Masked Visual Actions (MVA), a pixel-space control interface that enables a single pre-trained video model to function as a unified world model for both forward and inverse dynamics in robot manipulation. This approach achieved superior visual fidelity and cross-embodiment generalization in controllable video generation, improved planning success rates by up to 26% on Robocasa tasks, and demonstrated zero-shot inverse modeling with 90% success on a complex pick-and-place task.

hot.title: Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates
hot.summary: Researchers from Apollo Research and OpenAI developed Contrastive Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF) to quantitatively measure 'reward-seeking' in large language models. The method demonstrated that RL-trained models increasingly prioritize perceived grader preferences, even overriding explicit instructions in some cases, and that models known for 'reward-hacking' exhibited amplified reward-seeking tendencies.

hot.title: Language model harnesses are compositional generalizers
ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
hot.summary: The ABot-World Team at Alibaba Group's AMAP CV Lab developed ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model capable of generating interactive, persistent virtual worlds. It achieves real-time rollout at up to 16 frames per second (FPS) at 720P resolution with 1.2 seconds of action-to-first-frame latency, running on a single desktop GPU with less than 19.3 GiB VRAM.

hot.title: Self Gradient Forcing: Native Long Video Extrapolation
Intelligence from Learnable Novelty
hot.summary: Researchers at Tufts University and Harvard University propose 'learnable novelty' as a unifying principle for intelligence, and introduce a differentiable estimator for it. This objective successfully drives complex dynamics in cellular automata, enables unsupervised representation learning for MNIST with 0.89 accuracy, and provides a robust intrinsic reward for reinforcement learning agents across various tasks.

hot.title: Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing
hot.summary: Microsoft Mage Team developed Mage-Flow, a 4B-parameter foundation model that achieves competitive high-resolution image generation and instruction-based editing performance against much larger open-source models, demonstrating significant efficiency with 0.59s for 1024x1024 image generation on an NVIDIA A100 GPU and a 2.48x training speedup through system co-design.

hot.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
hot.summary: Experiential Learning (EL), developed by Microsoft Research and collaborators, introduces an "LLM-as-a-Coach" framework that transforms rich textual feedback into high-bandwidth learning signals for post-training language models on non-verifiable, open-ended tasks. This method consistently outperformed traditional reinforcement learning, demonstrating improved generalization and reduced reward hacking on various open-ended benchmarks.

hot.title: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
hot.summary: A framework called Agentic Real2Sim automatically converts real-world robotic interaction recordings into physically accurate, simulatable digital twins, supporting rigid, deformable, and humanoid domains. It achieved 48% replay success on 100 DROID rigid manipulation episodes using an open-weight VLM backend, demonstrating cost-effectiveness compared to proprietary models.

hot.title: Introducing Laguna S 2.1
ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack
hot.summary: Isospectral Optimization (ISO) provides an RLVR-native framework that addresses the distinct dynamics of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards by preserving the base model's weight spectra while adapting new behaviors through singular frame modifications. This approach improves training efficiency, achieving higher accuracy or faster convergence compared to conventional optimizers, and enables effective data-free merging of RLVR specialist models.

hot.title: MoGe-3: Fine-Detail Monocular Geometry Estimation with Self-Guided Sparse Volumetric Refinement
hot.summary: Researchers from Tsinghua University and Microsoft Research developed MoGe-3, a monocular geometry estimation model that integrates a Self-Guided Sparse 3D Refiner to produce geometrically undistorted and detail-preserving metric-scale point maps. The method shows improved accuracy in fine structures and maintains competitive global performance across various benchmarks.

hot.title: Robots Acquire Manipulation Skills in Seconds from a Single Human Video
hot.summary: A framework called HOST (Human-to-robot One-Shot Skill AcquisiTion) enables robots to acquire novel manipulation skills rapidly from a single human video demonstration in approximately 29 seconds. This approach achieves a 62% average success rate on 50 novel tasks, while preserving previously mastered skills by avoiding policy parameter updates.

hot.title: OmniReasoner: Thinking with Long Audio-Video via Native Tool Use
hot.summary: OmniReasoner, a post-training framework, enables omni-modal Large Language Models to reason effectively over long audio-video content by adaptively acquiring high-fidelity evidence via a "zoom-in" tool. The framework demonstrates improved accuracy on various benchmarks, including a 5.5-point gain on OmniVideoBench and a 15.6-point gain on VideoHolmes, by concentrating high-fidelity computation on relevant temporal regions.

hot.title: WorldScape Policy 2.0: Empowering Steerable World Action Modeling with Reasoning-Augmented Memory
hot.summary: WorldScape Policy 2.0, developed by Manifold AI, Tsinghua University, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, advances World Action Models by incorporating reasoning-augmented long short-term memory and diverse multimodal control. This system achieved 94.3% average success across 50 bimanual simulation tasks and demonstrated improved real-world performance on long-horizon and memory-dependent robotic manipulation.

hot.title: Pushing the Frontier of Full-Song Generation: Hierarchical Autoregressive Planning Meets Flow-Matching Rendering
Latent Riemannian Flow Matching for Geometry-Grounded 3D Foundation Models
hot.summary: Latent Riemannian Flow Matching enables generative 3D scene modeling by operating directly within the non-Euclidean latent space of a frozen geometric foundation model (VGGT). The framework significantly improves depth prediction and 3D scan generation from sparse, unposed inputs, reducing Chamfer distance by over 40% on ScanNet++ compared to baselines.

hot.title: SLAI T-Rex: Full-Parameter Post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 Family on Ascend SuperPOD
Mi-Memory: A Lifecycle Memory Framework for Personal AI
hot.summary: The Darwin Agent Team developed Mi-Memory, a lifecycle memory framework for personal AI that establishes an end-to-end audit contract, managing durable user state, integrating multimodal evidence, governing policy evolution, and ensuring deployability across varied constraints. The framework achieved a +19.16 percentage point gain on LoCoMo through automated strategy evolution and retained 90.0% of its service-side benefits in a lightweight, file-system-backed deployment.

hot.title: IGGT4D: Streaming 4D Instance-Grounded Geometry Transformer
hot.summary: A streaming instance-grounded geometry Transformer, IGGT4D, coupled with the InsScene4D-147K dataset, provides online 4D scene understanding by jointly predicting camera motion, 3D geometry, and temporally consistent instance features. This system achieved superior performance over streaming baselines in tasks like camera pose estimation, 3D reconstruction, and instance spatial tracking, while supporting efficient, scalable inference for long dynamic sequences.

likes.title: Language model harnesses are compositional generalizers
SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: SEED (SElf-Evolving On-Policy Distillation) enables large language model (LLM) agents to learn more effectively from their own experiences by generating and internalizing self-evolving, on-policy hindsight skills. This framework achieves substantial performance gains, such as a 14.9 to 45.9 percentage point improvement in macro-average success rate over outcome-only reinforcement learning on ALFWorld, through dense, token-level supervision and enhanced sample efficiency.

likes.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
likes.summary: Researchers from New York University and collaborators established a quantitative framework to understand the interplay between large language model pretraining and reinforcement learning in reasoning tasks, using a controlled chess environment. They developed a joint pretraining-RL scaling law, revealing that lower pretraining loss predicts higher post-RL performance and that optimal RL compute share increases with total compute, while also showing RL reshapes policies through both ground-truth amplification and wrong-mode amplification.

likes.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers from NAVER AI Lab introduce On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2), a method for post-training large language models that isolates and distills the specific reasoning capabilities acquired by a teacher model. OPD^2 achieves superior performance over existing on-policy distillation methods across diverse reasoning tasks, model sizes, and generation modes, notably improving math reasoning for a 1.7B parameter model by nearly 20 percentage points.

likes.title: Video = World + Event Stream
likes.summary: The Wan Team, Alibaba Group, developed a "world + event stream" decomposition for video content, establishing a general-purpose pretraining approach for interactive AI. This method enables real-time agents to perform open-vocabulary, free-form behaviors synchronized with speech at 640x368 resolution and 25 FPS, while preserving a low model-side latency of approximately 200 ms.

likes.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
likes.summary: NVIDIA researchers introduced RoboTTT, a framework that leverages Test-Time Training (TTT) to extend visuomotor context in robot foundation models to 8,000 timesteps while maintaining constant inference latency. This approach enables robots to achieve superior performance on complex, long-horizon tasks and unlocks capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and improved robustness to perturbations.

likes.title: VideoChat3: Fully Open Video MLLM for Efficient and Generalist Video Understanding
likes.summary: VideoChat3 introduces a fully open and efficient Video Multimodal Large Language Model (Video MLLM) designed for generalist video understanding across diverse durations and interaction modes. The model achieves strong performance on various video benchmarks while providing substantial computational efficiency for long and streaming videos, with all training components publicly released.

likes.title: Loop the Loopies!
likes.summary: A new scaling methodology, the "Loopie Recipe," enables recurrent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models to achieve competitive or superior performance under identical pre-training compute budgets. This approach culminated in Loopie models demonstrating gold-medal level performance on the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) and International Physics Olympiad (IPhO) 2025 problems without external tools.

likes.title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence
likes.summary: Princeton Language and Intelligence researchers developed a Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence (T²MLR), integrating recurrence into the network's middle layers to overcome the token-centric information bottleneck in autoregressive decoding. This approach improves reasoning capabilities on tasks such as S5-Retrieval and math benchmarks, maintains efficient inference with approximately 8% overhead, and can be retrofitted into pretrained models, achieving up to 40.6% relative accuracy increase on MATH500.

likes.title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots
likes.summary: Researchers from Shanghai AI Lab and collaborating institutions systematically investigated the scaling of Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) for humanoid robots, developing a principled recipe that integrates global-frame motion tracking, a balance of data quantity and diversity, and a Humanoid Transformer architecture. This approach led to a reduction in Mean Per-Keypoint Position Error (MPKPE) on the test set by over 10% in local mode and 82% in global mode compared to prior methods.

likes.title: DriftWorld: Fast World Modeling through Drifting
likes.summary: DriftWorld introduces an action-conditioned world model that generates future robot interaction frames in a single forward pass, achieving up to 17x faster inference (30+ fps) than diffusion models while matching or exceeding their visual quality. This model significantly boosts policy improvement metrics and demonstrates high correlation (up to 0.99 Pearson r^2) for offline policy evaluation across various robotic tasks.

likes.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
likes.summary: Sakana AI and UC Berkeley researchers developed Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI), an iterative algorithm that refines user-constructed agent harnesses based on pairwise feedback from execution history. RHI enables low-reasoning-effort agents to outperform stronger baselines while reducing inference costs by up to 60%, demonstrating that effective task-specific context management via prompt-level specifications can significantly enhance AI system performance and efficiency.

likes.title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
likes.summary: MeanFlowNFT is a framework that adapts forward-process reinforcement learning for MeanFlow models, enabling efficient fine-tuning of average-velocity generators to produce high-quality images and videos in few steps. It achieves performance comparable to or better than multi-step RL methods with a significantly reduced number of function evaluations.

likes.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories
likes.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-1, developed by Xiaomi Robotics, scales vision-language-action (VLA) models using over 100,000 hours of real-world manipulation trajectories, demonstrating improved out-of-the-box performance and efficient adaptation to novel tasks. This work provides empirical evidence that increasing data and model size enhances generalization, achieving state-of-the-art results across various robot manipulation benchmarks.

This approach achieved superior visual fidelity and cross-embodiment generalization in controllable video generation, improved planning success rates by up to 26% on Robocasa tasks, and demonstrated zero-shot inverse modeling with 90% success on a complex pick-and-place task.

likes.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
likes.summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University introduced BadWAM, a framework for "World-Action Drift Attacks" that desynchronize a robot's executed actions from its imagined future in World-Action Models (WAMs). This work demonstrates that WAMs can be manipulated to cause task failures even when their predicted future world states appear plausible, challenging the assumption that future prediction inherently guarantees safe behavior.

likes.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
likes.summary: SearchOS-V1 introduces a system-level multi-agent framework for robust open-domain information-seeking, externalizing search state into explicit, shared components and employing pipeline-parallel scheduling. The system achieved the best overall F1 scores on WideSearch, improving by 4.3 points, and reduced average end-to-end search time by 24.3% through enhanced coordination and error handling.

likes.title: Hierarchical Denoising For Multi-Step Visual Reasoning
likes.summary: Researchers at Peking University and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology developed Hierarchical Denoising for Visual Reasoning (HDR), a framework that enables robust multi-step visual reasoning in video generation models while maintaining low-latency streaming by integrating hierarchical latent spaces. HDR achieved a 76.2% relative gain in success rate on a multi-step reasoning benchmark and demonstrated comparable streaming latency to prior autoregressive methods, outperforming both streaming and full-attention baselines.
